subject: Context-silo billing and promotional discount interplay
messages:
From: Ben Lee <ben.lee@finapps.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-09T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot billing question — mixed long/short contexts + promo

Connor —

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. One follow-up from our engineering team: during our pilot we're going to send a mix of very long ingest requests (~18k tokens) and many short user-turn requests (~40–120 tokens) within the same conversation. You mentioned the promotional credit (20% off pilot usage) — we want to understand exactly how charges will be computed so we can forecast costs in our POC.

Key questions:
- Do you round each API call to a per-request quantum (e.g., nearest 10 tokens) or do you roll up at the conversation level?
- If we stream a long response (prefix heavy) and then have many small follow-ups, will the long request trigger a "minimum" that swamps the small calls?
- How does the promo discount apply — before or after rounding/minimums?

I've attached a short sample of our request log to illustrate (sample_request_log.csv). Can you provide a worked example with your current billing rules?

Best,
Ben
Sr. Product Manager
FinApps Inc.
(attachment: sample_request_log.csv)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Lee <ben.lee@finapps.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question — mixed long/short contexts + promo

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the log — super helpful. Short answer up front: by default our hosted billing rounds at a per-request level to the nearest 10-token quantum and enforces a 50-token per-request minimum for the hosted API SKU. Promo discounts are applied to the invoice line item subtotal after rounding and any minimums.

That default behavior is what most customers see, but we have two common levers for pilots:
1) Conversation-level aggregation: aggregate token use across a conversation for the purpose of rounding (one rollup per convo).
2) Pilot minimum waiver: temporarily lower the per-request minimum (e.g., 20 tokens) for the pilot window.

Below are two worked examples based on your sample:
- Example A (default): long ingest = 18,000 tokens -> rounded to 18,000 (quantum is negligible here), small calls of 45 tokens each -> each rounded to 50 due to minimum; subtotal = large + n*50; promo 20% applies to subtotal.
- Example B (conversation aggregation): aggregate total tokens for conversation = 18,000 + sum(small calls) -> apply rounding to the aggregate; promo then applied.

I'm looping in Aditya (billing) to confirm internal rounding implementation and Marissa for the commercial side. I've attached a short PDF with the illustrated math from our end (billing_examples.pdf).

Action: Aditya / Marissa, can you confirm how promo credits are recorded (invoice-level vs token-level) and whether we can enable conversation aggregation for the pilot?

Thanks,
Connor
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
(attachment: billing_examples.pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-09T13:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question — mixed long/short contexts + promo

Connor —

Confirming current hosted implementation and proposing a pilot rule:

Current hosted behavior (production):
- Metering: token counts are computed per API request (input + output tokens).
- Rounding: each request's token charge is rounded up to the nearest 10-token quantum.
- Minimum: if rounded token < 50, we bill 50 (per-request minimum).
- Promo application: promotional discounts are applied at invoice line-item subtotal (after all per-request rounding/minimums); accounting posts a discount line.

Worked example (from sample log):
- Long ingest request: 18,123 tokens -> rounded to 18,130 -> billed tokens = 18,130
- 10 follow-ups @ 45 tokens each -> each rounded to 50 (minimum) -> billed tokens = 10 * 50 = 500
- Subtotal billed tokens = 18,630 -> token price applied -> promo 20% off on dollar subtotal.

Proposal for pilot (FinApps) to better reflect your usage profile:
- Enable "conversation-level aggregation" flag for deal D-4729: aggregate tokens across a conversation before applying rounding (round the aggregate to nearest 10).
- Keep promo application at invoice subtotal (consistent with accounting).
- Pilot concession: waive per-request minimum for the duration, or replace it with an aggregate conversation floor of 100 tokens to prevent abuse.

If we enable aggregation, the same sample becomes: total tokens = 18,123 + (10 * 45) = 18,573 -> rounded to 18,570 (nearest 10) -> billed tokens = 18,570 -> fewer wasted minimums. Promo applies after.

I'll add the proposed rule to our billing runbook and attach the draft (proposed_aggregation_rule.md). If FinApps wants to proceed with the pilot behavior, legal needs to sign the amendment and finance will set the billing flag.

- Aditya
Lead, Billing & Pricing — Redwood Inference
(attachment: proposed_aggregation_rule.md)

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the patience. To keep the pilot moving forward we can offer the following commercial package for three months:

- Enable conversation-level aggregation for all concurrent conversations scoped to your pilot projects (will be flagged in billing for D-4729).
- Replace the per-request 50-token minimum with a per-conversation floor of 100 tokens (pre-rounding).
- Apply a 15% promotional discount to the resulting invoice subtotal (we're adjusting from the initial 20% ask to 15% in exchange for the aggregation concession).

Next steps:
